gateHistory: Initial test fixture issues (JPA isolation adapter and strict mock reads) were fixed. The full PostgreSQL/Common run passed all tests but failed scoped style on two migration-test formatting findings; those were corrected and the six selected architecture classes plus all scoped style and module boundaries then passed. Unchanged completed suites were not rerun just to obtain another aggregate log.
verifiedScenarios: Independent physical transactions and separate service instances serialize same-owner snapshots on empty and existing catalogs; final snapshot contains no interleaved leftover.
Competing owners recheck path ownership after lock acquisition; rollback releases lock without persisting its revision or resources.
Batch create, single/all/owner removal share the registration boundary; joined operations reuse one revision and roll back together.
Clean or dirty preloaded catalog entities, no transaction, read-only transaction, missing singleton row and older repeatable-read snapshots fail closed.
Plugin contribution install/uninstall competes with registration and retains outer rollback; owner removal protects foreign descendants even when closure rows are absent.
Actual V3-to-V4 migration preserves resource row values and revoked grants; rerunning migrations retains revision; constraints reject foreign singleton keys and negative revisions.
Actual shared/separate module storage assembly binds the new boundary to identity persistence; affected full migration, packaged persistence, repository ownership and remote-contract checks pass.
Actual module JAR contains exact V4 script, manifest and write boundary; resource implementation artifact contains both error locales.
limitations: Concurrency uses separate services and database transactions inside one JVM, not independently deployed JVMs; the lock itself is the PostgreSQL row update.

Resource database tests use the real V4 script and ORM-created remaining tables. Migration/ownership tests separately use the actual module installer. Grant/tenant provision collaborators in resource tests remain mocks.

Existing three large Common read-only HTTP fixtures received only the constructor dependency mock; their existing full tests passed. Scoped Checkstyle covers 14 implementation/new-or-formatted test files, not those three pre-existing fixture files.

No production database/configuration write, deployment, service distribution rebuild, commit or push in this increment. Actual checked artifacts are module JARs, not a newly installed service distribution.

Catalog revision is not deployment generation. Old instances must be retired during coordinated upgrade; legacy schema adoption, generation fencing, stale-owner adoption and formal installer remain incomplete.

Preloaded catalog persistence contexts must be redesigned to enter the boundary before reads; no automatic clear or silent context refresh is used. Direct SQL and other independent management paths are not implicitly protected.
Formal standalone host, remaining HTTP/frontend/authorization composition and complete three-topology business/browser/failure acceptance remain required.
